context: This perfect binary tree has 15 nodes on 4 levels. In level order, their values run from 1 to 15. Level 1 holds root 1, level 2 holds 2 and 3, level 3 holds 4 through 7, and level 4 holds leaves 8 through 15. The array stores them in that order at indices 0 through 14. The table lists each node's index and the positions of its children.

frames.explanation: Use the array index i in the formulas. For example, node 6 is at index 5. Its left child is at index 11 (value 12), and its right child is at index 12 (value 13).
frames.title: Array representation of a perfect binary tree

result: The index formulas can take the place of child pointers, but access still requires a bounds check. Indices 7 through 14 hold leaves (nodes 8 through 15). Their calculated child positions, 15 through 30, are all out of bounds, indicating that these nodes have no children.
summary: Store a perfect binary tree in level order in a zero-based array. For a node at index i, use 2i+1 and 2i+2 to locate its left and right children.
title: Array representation of a perfect binary tree
